1. Why the original 100 % was not a valid estimate

The original script reached accuracy 1.000 on a single random split with only 11 AI test clips, where always answering "human" already scores 0.917. 11 of 11 AI test files were re-voicings of a source recording that was also in training. With the same features and model, group-aware CV gives balanced accuracy 0.735 ± 0.115 and leave-one-source-speaker-out gives 0.758 ± 0.167.

2. Data

2126 files; 2564 analysis windows after 94 files were skipped (too_short: 91, silent: 3). User data alone fails the adequacy checks (independent AI groups: 8; AI generators: 1). Supplementary data: ASVspoof 2019 LA subset (ODC-By licence), adding 19 spoofing systems.

3. Model comparison (nested, group-aware 5-fold CV on the development partition)

Hyperparameters were tuned by inner group-aware CV on each outer training fold only. The selection rule was fixed before results were inspected: Primary metric: mean outer-fold ROC-AUC (group-aware 5-fold CV, dev partition only). Candidates whose paired group-bootstrap 95% CI for (best - candidate) pooled OOF AUC includes 0 are tied with the best; among tied candidates the simplest is chosen (model: logreg < linear_svm < rbf_svm < rbf_svm_original < random_forest < hist_gb; features: baseline < extended). The deployed model is trained on user + supplementary data unless its out-of-fold AUC on user-domain rows is more than 0.02 below the user-only model's.

Selected: Hist. gradient boosting on extended features, trained on User + supplementary (ASVspoof 2019 LA). Best mean AUC in that setting: Hist. gradient boosting / extended (0.966). First augmentation rule (MP3 only): adopted False. Deployed training augmentation: mp3cv. Calibration: sigmoid.

Robustness-aware augmentation study (development data only)

The test-set robustness analysis of the model chosen by the clean-data rule showed that added noise or microphone-like processing made it label almost all human speech as AI. This study was run afterwards, so the deployed model's test results are post-hoc (see VERIFICATION_REPORT).

Rule (fixed before the study ran): Maximise mean validation ROC-AUC over conditions ['clean', 'mp3', 'white20', 'room20', 'mic'] (validation windows perturbed; development data only), among candidates whose clean AUC is within 0.02 of no augmentation; candidates within 0.002 of the best are tied and the one with fewer augmentation types wins. Augmented copies are used in training folds only. Chosen: mp3.

4. Calibration and decision threshold

A false alarm (a real person's voice labelled synthetic) is treated as twice as costly as a missed synthetic voice, because acting on a false accusation harms a real person, whereas a miss leaves the status quo. The threshold minimising expected cost on out-of-fold validation predictions is used; an inconclusive band of +/- 0.15 around it is shown in the UI. Chosen threshold: 0.64; inconclusive band 0.49-0.79 (on validation predictions 13.1% of windows fall inside it; accuracy outside it 0.928).

5. Held-out test set

Test groups never appeared in development: user source speakers biden, taylor (all 14 of their conversions); 9 of 56 Common Voice run-groups (154 of 605 clips); and the ASVspoof evaluation partition (625 files, 67 speakers, systems A07, A08, A09, A10, A11, A12, A13, A14, A15, A16, A17, A18, A19).

The pre-registered model was chosen before any test evaluation; its rows are the primary result. The deployed model was chosen afterwards by the development-data robustness study (section 3), so its test rows are post-hoc.

6. Generalisation

Trained on all 19 ASVspoof systems but not on the user's conversion tool, the model flags 0.0% of the user's 560 AI windows (ROC-AUC 0.478); trained on the user's data only, it reaches ROC-AUC 0.541 on ASVspoof. Detection does not transfer to unseen generators or datasets.

10. Limitations and ethics

  • The user's AI audio comes from a single (unknown) voice-conversion tool and 8 source recordings; the human audio is crowd-sourced Common Voice MP3. Recording channel differs systematically between the classes, so part of what any model learns may be channel rather than synthesis.
  • Common Voice speaker identities are unavailable; human groups are inferred from clip-ID runs (low-medium confidence).
  • ASVspoof 2019 systems date from 2019; modern generators are not covered. Detectors can be fooled by unseen generators, post-processing and adversarial edits.
  • Microphone recordings differ from all training data (room acoustics, browser processing); treat live results as indicative only.
  • Accent, language and recording-device bias are not measured. Never use this output as the sole evidence against a person.
